annotations.description: Cast Seam Rip on turn 1 when the opponent has no nonland permanents on the battlefield. Seam Rip's ETB trigger requires targeting a nonland permanent an opponent controls with mana value 2 or less, but there are none. annotations.description: GPT5n used Get Lost to destroy the opponent's Seam Rip instead of Enduring Innocence. Seam Rip is exiling one of GPT5n's permanents (likely a small creature or permanent), but Enduring Innocence is a much more dangerous threat - it's a 2/1 lifelink creature that draws cards whenever small creatures enter, and it returns as an enchantment when it dies (though Rest in Peace would exile it instead). With Rest in Peace in play, Get Lost on Enduring Innocence would permanently remove it since it would be exiled instead of returning. Meanwhile, destroying Seam Rip gives the opponent two Map tokens and only recovers whatever was exiled. Enduring Innocence is the key card advantage engine that will generate significant value over the course of the game, especially since the opponent has token generation (Fountainport, and potentially Ajani). Additionally, GPT5n has Day of Judgment in hand which could handle creatures later, but removing the card advantage engine now while Rest in Peace ensures it stays dead is the stronger line.

annotations.betterLine: Target Enduring Innocence with Get Lost. With Rest in Peace on the battlefield, Enduring Innocence would be exiled instead of going to the graveyard, preventing its return-to-battlefield trigger. This permanently removes the opponent's card advantage engine.

annotations.description: High Noon limits each player to one spell per turn. GLM47 Snark has Enduring Curiosity (a powerful 4/3 flash creature with card draw) and Ajani in hand, plus Enduring Innocence on board that draws cards when small creatures enter. High Noon symmetrically locks both players to one spell per turn, but GLM47 has a hand full of impactful spells (Enduring Curiosity, Ajani, Seam Rip) that they'll now be unable to deploy quickly. The opponent has an empty board except for enchantments (two Seam Rips exiling something), so they're not casting many spells anyway. Playing Ajani instead would create tokens (triggering Enduring Innocence for card draw) and apply pressure, which seems more impactful than a symmetrical lock that hurts GLM47's own development more than the opponent's current position.
